physicochemical properties of drug molecules due to its high
electronegativity and small size.<sup>1</sup> Additionally, the introduction

metabolic stability, and membrane permeability of the
molecules, thereby improving their eficacy and pharmacoki-
netic properties.<sup>2</sup> In recent years, gem-difluoroalkenes have
attracted much attention in the field of medicinal chemistry<sup>3</sup> as
a bioisostere of carbonyl group, which could efectively
improve the metabolic stability of molecules and optimize
the biological activity by modulating the electronic properties
of the target binding sites.<sup>4</sup> For instance, the replacement of
the carbonyl group in the artemisinin molecule by a gem-
difluoroalkene moiety significantly enhanced the antimalarial
activity, suggesting that its structure showed efects on the
interaction of the molecule with the biological targets based on
the adjustment of the electronic distribution and spatial
conformation. Furthermore, the gem-difluoroalkene moiety
exhibited unique electronic properties and could be employed

drugs making it a versatile module in drug design (Scheme
1A).<sup>5</sup>

■ CONCLUSION
In summary, we have developed a novel palladium-catalyzed β-
selective hydrosilylation of gem-difluoroallenes with hydro-
silanes, providing eficient access to gem-difluorovinylsilanes.
This method exhibits a broad substrate scope, delivering the
target products in moderate to excellent yields, and
demonstrates excellent compatibility with late-stage function-
alization strategies. Mechanistic investigations through density
functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed the key
transition states, ofering fundamental insights into the origin
of the observed chemo- and regioselectivity. Given the mild
reaction conditions and operational simplicity of this protocol,
the resulting β-difluorovinylsilanes and their derivatives hold
significant potential for diverse applications in synthetic
chemistry and pharmaceutical research.
